articles.title: Srikanth Saves Three Match Points and Outlasts Okimoto to Reach the US Open Final
articles.excerpt: The former world No. 1 rallied from a game down to beat Japan’s Yudai Okimoto 22-20, 15-21, 21-19 in Fullerton, setting up a California title showdown with Chinese Taipei’s Su Li-yang on Sunday
articles.image_caption: Kidambi Srikanth in action during a BWF World Tour event
articles.nri_angle: Tournament played in Fullerton, California — heart of Southern California’s Indian-American community — with Srikanth competing for a title on the diaspora’s doorstep during a packed US sports summer.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Last Innings? Inside the Growing Debate Over Rohit Sharma's Place in India's 2027 World Cup Plans
articles.excerpt: Reports suggest chief selector Ajit Agarkar and coach Gautam Gambhir are not building their long-term ODI strategy around the 39-year-old former captain — but neither will they say so directly
articles.image_caption: Rohit Sharma batting during the India vs Australia Test match at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad, in 2023.
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs across the United States, United Kingdom, and Canada, Rohit Sharma has been the face of India's ODI golden age — the captain who lifted the 2025 Champions Trophy. The debate over his future touches on the deep emotional bond between the diaspora and Indian cricket's biggest names, and raises questions about whether the next generation can carry the same weight for fans watching from abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pooran's Unbeaten 70 and Kenjige's Three-For Demolish the Knight Riders in Oakland
articles.excerpt: Nicholas Pooran anchored MI New York's 144 with an unbeaten half-century, then Nosthush Kenjige — the Hyderabad-born left-arm spinner who grew up in the American cricket system — tore through LA Knight Riders' batting to bowl them out for 103 at the Oakland Coliseum.
articles.image_caption: Oakland Coliseum, the Bay Area home of Major League Cricket's 2026 season
articles.nri_angle: MLC's Bay Area matches at the Oakland Coliseum give NRIs across Silicon Valley and the wider diaspora a rare chance to watch world-class cricket live in the US, with Indian-American players like Kenjige starring on American soil.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: She Cleared 4.25 Metres and Broke a Record That Was Only Days Old. Indian Women's Pole Vault Has Arrived.
articles.excerpt: Karnataka's Sindhushree G set a new national record at the Inter-State Championships in Bhubaneswar, beating rival Baranica Elangovan's mark and qualifying for the Asian Games — part of a week that saw national records fall across five disciplines.
articles.image_caption: Kalinga Stadium in Bhubaneswar, venue of the 65th National Inter-State Senior Athletics Championships
articles.nri_angle: The Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya and the Glasgow Commonwealth Games give NRIs in North America, Europe, and Japan front-row seats to India's athletics breakthrough, with several newly qualified women athletes set to compete on the global stage.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Indians Storm US Open Badminton Semifinals as Srikanth, Teen Prodigy Rounak, and Devika Sihag Shine in California
articles.excerpt: Former world No. 1 Kidambi Srikanth leads a three-strong Indian charge into the last four at Fullerton, joined by 18-year-old qualifier Rounak Chouhan and Thailand Masters champion Devika Sihag
articles.image_caption: Kidambi Srikanth in action during a BWF tournament
articles.image_credit: Pierre-Yves Beaudouin / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 4.0
articles.nri_angle: Three Indians reach semifinals at a BWF Super 300 event in Fullerton, California — the heart of Southern California's Indian-American community — with the prospect of an all-Indian men's singles final on Sunday.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Sound of His Bat Was Like a Gunshot': Sangakkara Recalls the Day He Discovered Sooryavanshi
articles.excerpt: Speaking on Sky Sports Cricket during the India-Ireland broadcast, the Rajasthan Royals director of cricket described a training-camp net session in Guwahati where a 14-year-old put Jofra Archer and Sandeep Sharma to the sword — and left even the fast bowlers stunned.
articles.image_caption: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi meets Prime Minister Narendra Modi after his record-breaking IPL 2026 season
articles.nri_angle: Sooryavanshi's rise from cricket-backwater Bihar to IPL stardom resonates with millions of NRIs who follow the league in 120+ countries — a testament to raw talent breaking through regardless of geography.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The World Cup Arrives in Santa Clara on Wednesday. It May Never Be This Close Again.
articles.excerpt: When the USA faces Bosnia and Herzegovina at Levi’s Stadium on July 1, the knockout stage comes to the doorstep of one of the largest Indian-American communities in the United States.
articles.image_caption: Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara, California, the venue for the USA’s Round of 32 World Cup match on July 1
articles.nri_angle: The World Cup’s only Bay Area knockout match brings the tournament to the doorstep of one of America’s largest Indian-American communities, giving NRIs in Silicon Valley a rare chance to experience the biggest sporting event on the planet without leaving home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'Sadly, Cricket Wasn’t Part of It Then': Harmanpreet Kaur Sets Her Sights on LA 2028
articles.excerpt: India’s World Cup-winning captain invoked Milkha Singh’s legacy as she spoke about her dream of leading the country at cricket’s Olympic debut in Los Angeles — a city where millions of Indian Americans could watch it happen.
articles.image_caption: Harmanpreet Kaur with the 2025 Women’s Cricket World Cup trophy
articles.nri_angle: Cricket returns to the Olympics at LA 2028, giving millions of Indian Americans in Southern California the chance to watch India play the sport in a global multi-sport event for the first time — in their own city.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Isn't Playing at the World Cup. It Might Be the Tournament's Biggest Audience Anyway.
articles.excerpt: With 305 million football fans, Bollywood on European club feeds, and 300 million streaming viewers, the diaspora and India's digital-first generation are reshaping how the world sells the beautiful game — all without a team on the pitch.
articles.image_caption: Fans celebrate at a FIFA World Cup 2026 match in the United States
articles.nri_angle: With matches across US cities home to large NRI populations, and India's 305-million-strong football audience driving record streaming numbers, the World Cup is on the diaspora's doorstep for the first time.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Seven Goals, Seven Scorers: India Tear Pakistan Apart in London
articles.excerpt: India produced a second-half masterclass at Lee Valley, hammering Pakistan 7-1 in the FIH Pro League to complete a memorable double and extend a decade-long unbeaten run against their arch-rivals.
articles.image_caption: The Indian men's hockey team, who demolished Pakistan 7-0 in their FIH Pro League clash in London (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Rare chance for UK-based Indian diaspora to watch India play live at Lee Valley in London; India's dominant hockey form is a source of pride for NRIs worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Rajasthan Royals Star Hit 87 off 39 Balls in Texas. The MLC’s Match of the Season Was Only Getting Started.
articles.excerpt: Lhuan-dre Pretorius tore apart Seattle’s bowling, Brody Couch sealed it with a boundary off the final over, and San Francisco Unicorns climbed to the top of the MLC standings with a two-wicket thriller at Grand Prairie.
articles.image_caption: Grand Prairie Stadium in Texas, the converted former ballpark that now serves as Major League Cricket’s spiritual home, hosted the MLC’s match of the season.
articles.nri_angle: MLC targets NRI fans; Pretorius plays for Rajasthan Royals in IPL; Indian-American batter Sanjay Krishnamurthy in Unicorns XI; Indian-American umpire Vijaya Mallela on MLC panel; Grand Prairie in Dallas-Fort Worth is a major Indian-American population hub; IPL franchise connections deepen the league’s relevance.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mirabai Chanu Will Lead India's Weightlifting Charge at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games
articles.excerpt: The Olympic silver medallist headlines a seven-strong squad for Glasgow 2026, with Birmingham medallists Bindyarani Devi and Harjinder Kaur also named. Four debutants join the team.
articles.image_caption: Olympic silver medallist Mirabai Chanu, who will lead India's weightlifting squad at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow
articles.nri_angle: Glasgow 2026 is the most accessible major multi-sport event for UK-based NRIs; Chanu returns to the city where she won her first Commonwealth medal in 2014.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: He Came Through Qualifying and Saved Four Match Points. Then the Top Seed Was Out.
articles.excerpt: Rounak Chouhan, 18, ranked 80th in the world, stunned tournament No. 1 seed Chou Tien Chen in straight games to lead India's surge at the US Open badminton in Fullerton, California.
articles.image_caption: Kidambi Srikanth, who added to India's dominant day with a commanding win over Malaysia's Lee Zii Jia
articles.nri_angle: The US Open badminton tournament in Fullerton, California, is offering Indian-Americans a rare chance to watch India's top shuttlers compete live — and 18-year-old Rounak Chouhan's giant-killing run is the tournament's standout story.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Thirteen Athletes Qualified in a Single Day. The Triple Jumpers Were the Story India Didn't See Coming.
articles.excerpt: Six of the top six men's triple jumpers all cleared the Asian Games mark at Bhubaneswar — Praveen Chithravel led with a 16.92m opener — as Day 3 of the Inter-State Championships showed just how deep India's track and field talent pool has become
articles.image_caption: Praveen Chithravel competing in the triple jump at the 2018 Summer Youth Olympics in Buenos Aires
articles.nri_angle: India is producing world-class depth in track and field events for the first time, a transformation diaspora sports fans who watched the country struggle outside cricket will find striking.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kohli Is Back, Jaiswal Is Out, and India Have Named Their ODI Squad for England
articles.excerpt: Shubman Gill leads a 15-member squad for the three-match series starting July 14 — with Virat Kohli's return squeezing out the man who scored a century in his absence
articles.image_caption: Virat Kohli in India cricket whites during an international match
articles.nri_angle: With nearly 2 million Indians in the UK, the summer cricket tour — featuring Kohli's return — is a pilgrimage-level event for NRI fans, and the series overlaps with peak diaspora travel season.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Five Sixes in an Over: Marcus Stoinis Rips Washington Freedom Apart as Seattle Orcas Cruise to an 88-Run MLC Victory
articles.excerpt: Shimron Hetmyer's nine-six blitz and Jasdeep Singh's five-wicket masterclass power the biggest win of MLC 2026 at the Oakland Coliseum
articles.image_caption: Marcus Stoinis batting for Australia in a T20 International
articles.nri_angle: MLC brings high-quality professional cricket to American venues like the Oakland Coliseum, with Indian-heritage players like Jasdeep Singh starring in the Bay Area — the heart of the NRI community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: John Abraham Bets on European Cricket — and Joins Jonty Rhodes and Faf du Plessis at the Rotterdam Dockers
articles.excerpt: The Bollywood actor becomes co-owner of a Rotterdam franchise in the inaugural European T20 Premier League, cricket's first ICC-backed multi-nation league in Europe
articles.image_caption: Bollywood actor and sports entrepreneur John Abraham
articles.nri_angle: The ETPL brings live franchise cricket to Europe for the first time, offering NRIs in the Netherlands, Ireland, and Scotland a home-turf cricket experience backed by Bollywood star power.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Wimbledon 2026: India's Hopes Ride on Yuki Bhambri and the Doubles Brigade
articles.excerpt: With no Indian in the singles draw, a top-20 Bhambri leads a seasoned doubles contingent onto the SW19 grass when the Championships begin Monday.
articles.image_caption: Yuki Bhambri, India's top-ranked doubles player at world No. 18, leads the country's contingent at Wimbledon 2026.
articles.nri_angle: Wimbledon is the most accessible Grand Slam for the Indian diaspora in the UK, US, Canada and Australia, and in 2026 the tricolour is carried almost entirely by world No. 18 doubles player Yuki Bhambri and India's doubles specialists rather than any singles entrant.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: San Francisco Get Their Revenge on Texas — by the Width of a Single Run
articles.excerpt: Defending just 148, the Bay Area's Major League Cricket franchise held its nerve to the final ball in Lauderhill, where a run-out off the last delivery sealed a one-run win over the Texas Super Kings — and turned an early defeat into a statement.
articles.image_caption: Marcus Stoinis, who took 3-32 for the Texas Super Kings before they fell one run short against the San Francisco Unicorns.
articles.nri_angle: The San Francisco Unicorns are the Bay Area's own Major League Cricket franchise, and the region's huge Indian-origin tech community — with R Ashwin now in the squad — finally has a top-tier team to follow in person, making a last-ball thriller like this a milestone in cricket's American growth.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ireland Beat India for the First Time — and They Picked the Perfect Day to Do It
articles.excerpt: In Shreyas Iyer's first match as captain, India were bowled out for 148 chasing 183 in Belfast, handing Ireland a maiden win over a side they had never beaten in 11 internationals — and turning the start of a new era into a reckoning.
articles.image_caption: India captain Shreyas Iyer, whose first match in charge ended in a maiden defeat to Ireland in Belfast.
articles.nri_angle: This India team is followed match by match across the US, UK and Canada, and the post-World-Cup transition under new captain Shreyas Iyer is a story the diaspora is deeply invested in — making a first-ever defeat to Ireland, a side many NRIs live alongside, both a shock and a sign that the new India will have to earn its aura rather than inherit it.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Must Beat the Unbeaten: A Lord's Date With Australia Will Decide Their World Cup
articles.excerpt: Australia have won every match and can afford to lose; India cannot. Sunday's group finale at Lord's is, in effect, a quarterfinal India have to win to reach the last four.
articles.image_caption: India captain Harmanpreet Kaur with the 2025 Women's Cricket World Cup trophy

articles.nri_angle: A women's World Cup knockout-in-all-but-name at Lord's gives Indian fans across the US, UK, Canada and Australia a marquee stage to rally behind a generation of stars — Mandhana, Shafali and Harmanpreet — their daughters can grow up idolising.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Teenage Shooters Are Topping a World Championship in Germany — and Rewriting the Record Book
articles.excerpt: At the ISSF Junior World Championship in Suhl, India leads the medal table with five golds, while a 10m air rifle pair set a new junior world record — a preview of the talent pipeline aimed at Los Angeles 2028.
articles.image_caption: An Indian junior in the 10m air rifle final at a youth world shooting event, the same discipline in which India's teenagers topped the ISSF Junior World Championship in Suhl.
articles.image_credit: Martin Rulsch, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
articles.nri_angle: Shooting has quietly become India's most reliable Olympic medal factory, and the teenagers topping the ISSF Junior World Championship in Suhl — a junior world record included — are the names NRIs should learn now, because they are the ones aimed at the Los Angeles 2028 Games.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Down 0-4 to a Bullet Specialist, Arjun Erigaisi Won the Next 16 — and a Shot at the World's Fastest Chess Title
articles.excerpt: India's No. 1 thrashed two-time runner-up Andrew Tang 16-6 to reach the Bullet Chess Championship Winners Final, with Nihal Sarin still alive in the bracket — the clearest sign yet that India now owns the fastest format in the game.
articles.image_caption: Indian grandmaster Arjun Erigaisi, who beat Andrew Tang 16-6 to reach the Winners Final of the 2026 Bullet Chess Championship.
articles.nri_angle: Online speed chess is where the diaspora watches India's golden generation in real time — free global streams, results in minutes — and Arjun Erigaisi one win from a Grand Final in the world's fastest format, alongside Nihal Sarin, is exactly the bite-sized Indian triumph NRIs rally around and share.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: One Year After the Injury That Cost Her a Season, Jyothi Yarraji Is Back Under 13 Seconds
articles.excerpt: At the National Inter-State Championships in Bhubaneswar, India's first Olympic 100m hurdler ran 12.99 to win gold — the number she had been chasing since a knee injury wiped out much of her 2025.
articles.image_caption: The Kalinga Stadium in Bhubaneswar, host of the 65th National Inter-State Senior Athletics Championships, where Jyothi Yarraji ran 12.99 to win the 100m hurdles.
articles.image_credit: Government of Odisha, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0)
articles.nri_angle: For an Indian diaspora that has learned to follow Olympic track and field through Neeraj Chopra, Jyothi Yarraji is the next name to know — the first Indian woman to run the 100m hurdles at a Games — and her comeback from a season-ending injury, capped by a sub-13 run in Bhubaneswar, is exactly the arc NRI sports fans rally behind ahead of the Asian Games.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An 18-Year-Old With an Indian Flag on His Helmet Is the Closest Thing F1 Has Had to India in 15 Years
articles.excerpt: Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad — born to a British-Indian mother and a Swedish father — arrives at this weekend's Austrian Grand Prix as the only driver of Indian heritage on the grid since Karun Chandhok in 2011.
articles.image_caption: Arvid Lindblad, the 18-year-old Racing Bulls rookie of Indian and Swedish heritage, in Melbourne during the 2026 Formula 1 season.
articles.nri_angle: Arvid Lindblad, born to a British-Indian mother, is the first driver of Indian heritage on the Formula 1 grid since Karun Chandhok in 2011 — giving the diaspora a reason to follow the sport again as he races this weekend in Austria.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Shuttlers Have Brought Their Season to California — and Opened the US Open With a Near-Clean Sweep
articles.excerpt: From veteran Kidambi Srikanth to 17-year-old Tanvi Sharma, India's badminton contingent swept through the first round of the US Open in Fullerton, a Super 300 event staged on the doorstep of one of America's largest South Asian communities.
articles.image_caption: Kidambi Srikanth in action; the former world No. 1 is the No. 5 seed in India's US Open contingent in Fullerton, California.
articles.nri_angle: A full-strength Indian badminton contingent is competing in a sanctioned BWF event on US soil in Fullerton, California, putting the country's shuttlers within driving distance of one of America's largest South Asian communities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Big-League Cricket Has Moved Into the Oakland Coliseum — and the Bay Area's Team Lost the First Round
articles.excerpt: Major League Cricket's fourth season has turned the old A's ballpark into the home of the playoffs and the final, but the San Francisco Unicorns opened their Oakland stand with a 22-run defeat to the Texas Super Kings.
articles.image_caption: An aerial view of the Oakland Coliseum, which is hosting Major League Cricket matches, the playoffs and the 2026 final.
articles.nri_angle: Major League Cricket has brought top-flight T20 cricket — and its 2026 playoffs and final — to the Oakland Coliseum, putting international-calibre players within a short drive of the Bay Area's large South Asian diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Shafali Verma Drags India Out of the Danger Zone — and Into a Sunday Showdown With Australia
articles.excerpt: A 34-ball 53 anchored India's five-wicket chase of Bangladesh at Old Trafford, a must-win that keeps them second in a three-way logjam and sets up a final group decider against the unbeaten champions at Lord's.
articles.image_caption: Shafali Verma, whose 34-ball 53 anchored India's chase against Bangladesh at the Women's T20 World Cup.
articles.nri_angle: The Women's T20 World Cup is being played on English grounds, putting India's title defence within reach of diaspora fans across the UK — with Sunday's decisive group game against Australia at Lord's.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A New Captain, and a 15-Year-Old Knocking: India Begin the Iyer Era in Belfast
articles.excerpt: Shreyas Iyer leads India for the first time in Friday's opening T20I against Ireland, and the toughest call of his debut is whether to break up a World Cup-winning top three to fit teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.
articles.image_caption: Shreyas Iyer, who captains India in T20Is for the first time against Ireland in Belfast.
articles.nri_angle: The two-match series is played on diaspora doorsteps in the British Isles and offers NRIs a first look at India under new T20I captain Shreyas Iyer, plus the possible international debut of 15-year-old viral sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: One Centimetre, and the Record Is His Alone: Dev Meena Vaults to 5.46m
articles.excerpt: The 21-year-old from Madhya Pradesh cleared 5.46m at the National Inter-State Championships in Bhubaneswar, breaking the men's pole vault national record he had shared with his training partner and booking his ticket to the Asian Games.
articles.image_caption: Indian pole vaulter Dev Meena, who broke the men's national record with a clearance of 5.46m.
articles.nri_angle: Pole vault has rarely featured in NRI sports conversations, but Dev Meena's record run and dual Asian Games and Commonwealth Games qualification give diaspora fans a new Indian track-and-field name to follow as both Games approach.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Women Won a Trophy and a Promotion in One Night in Auckland
articles.excerpt: Two first-quarter penalty corners beat hosts New Zealand 2-0 in the FIH Hockey Women's Nations Cup final, handing Salima Tete's unbeaten side the title and a direct return to the elite Pro League barely a year after relegation.
articles.image_caption: India captain Salima Tete, who led the team to an unbeaten FIH Hockey Women's Nations Cup title in Auckland.
articles.nri_angle: India's women returning to the FIH Pro League means diaspora fans across Europe and beyond will get far more chances to watch the national team play live next season, as Pro League fixtures tour host cities worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Have Never Won at Edgbaston. Now They Must — and Decide Whether to Risk Bumrah to Do It
articles.excerpt: Trailing England 0-1, Shubman Gill's young side arrives in Birmingham for the second Test on July 2 facing a green pitch, a venue that has beaten India eight times out of eight, and the recurring question of whether to spend their best bowler now or save him for Lord's.
articles.image_caption: India pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah, whose availability for the Edgbaston Test is the central selection question of the tour.
articles.nri_angle: Edgbaston sits in the heart of Britain's largest South Asian community, making the second Test the closest thing to a home game for UK-based Indian fans — a rare in-person chance to watch Shubman Gill's new-look side try to level the series and finally win at the one English ground that has always beaten India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
